t: What a Compressed Air Duster Can Is
title: What a Compressed Air Duster Can Is
description: A compressed air duster can is a 10-ounce can of liquefied gas (usually difluoroethane) that blasts a high-pressure stream when you press the trigger — the standard tool for blowing dust out of PC cases, fans, heatsinks, and keyboards. The gas boils to vapor as it leaves, giving a strong, dry, residue-free blast. Every PC bench needs one; dust is the silent performance killer.

demo.program:
print("Can: 10 oz liquefied difluoroethane -> trigger -> high-pressure dry blast.")
print("Jobs: cases, fans, heatsinks, keyboards, filters.")
print("Dust = silent performance killer (heat + noise). Every bench needs one.")

t: How the Gas Blast Works: Liquid to Vapor
title: How the Gas Blast Works: Liquid to Vapor
description: The can holds gas liquefied under pressure; pressing the trigger releases liquid that instantly boils into vapor, and the expansion drives the blast at around 70 psi. The phase change chills the can — that is why cans get cold and why liquid sometimes sprays if you tilt. Short bursts keep the pressure strong; long sprays drain pressure as the can chills.

demo.program:
print("Liquid under pressure -> trigger -> boils to vapor -> ~70 psi blast.")
print("Phase change chills the can: cold can = weak pressure.")
print("Short bursts stay strong; long sprays chill out and weaken.")
print("Tilt = liquid spray (freezing, can leave residue): keep upright.")

t: Technique: Short Bursts, Upright Can, Outside Air
title: Technique: Short Bursts, Upright Can, Outside Air
description: The technique: can upright always, short 1-2 second bursts, nozzle a few inches from the target, and work with the case outdoors or in ventilated space — the dust has to go somewhere. Blast heatsinks fin-by-fin from the clean side out, hold fan blades still while blowing (spinning them generates voltage), and finish with filters and intakes.

print("Upright can, 1-2s bursts, nozzle inches from target.")
print("Work outdoors/ventilated: the dust has to GO somewhere.")
print("Hold fan blades STILL (spinning = generates voltage into the board).")
print("Heatsinks: fin by fin, clean side outward. Finish: filters + intakes.")

t: Use Case: Heatsink and Fan Deep Clean
title: Use Case: Heatsink and Fan Deep Clean
description: Clogged heatsink fins can raise CPU temps 10-20°C — a full cleaning restores performance you forgot you had. Remove the side panel, take the case outside, hold each fan still, and blast fins from inside out so dust exits the case instead of deeper in. For caked fins, loosen with a soft brush first, then blast. Check temps before and after: the difference is the proof.

demo.program:
before, after = 87, 71
print(f"CPU temp before: {before}C, after deep clean: {after}C (delta {before-after}C)")
print("Method: outside, fans held still, fins inside-out, brush first if caked.")
print("Clogged fins cost 10-20C: cleaning restores forgotten performance.")

title: Use Case: Keyboard, Ports, and Crevice Cleaning

t: Safety: The Bittering Agent, Inhalation, and Frostbite
title: Safety: The Bittering Agent, Inhalation, and Frostbite
description: Duster gas contains a bittering agent to discourage inhalation — deliberately inhaling it (dusting) is dangerous and can be fatal; the cans warn clearly. Liquid spray causes frostbite on skin — never spray skin, and keep the can upright. Use in ventilated areas; the gas displaces oxygen in enclosed spaces. These are serious warnings on a casual-looking can: read and respect them.

demo.program:
print("Bittering agent: deters abuse. Inhalant abuse (dusting) can be FATAL.")
print("Liquid spray = frostbite: never on skin, can upright always.")
print("Ventilated areas only: gas displaces oxygen in enclosed spaces.")
print("Casual-looking can, serious warnings: read and respect them.")

t: The Tilt Problem: Why Liquid Sprays and How to Avoid It
title: The Tilt Problem: Why Liquid Sprays and How to Avoid It
description: Tilt the can past about 30 degrees and liquid (not vapor) reaches the valve — spraying freezing liquid that can thermal-shock components and leave residue. Keep the can upright; for angled shots into tight spots, bend your wrist not the can, or use the straw to redirect. If liquid does spray on a board, let it evaporate fully before powering on.

demo.program:
print("Tilt >~30 deg: liquid hits valve -> freezing spray (thermal shock + residue).")
print("Fix: can upright ALWAYS; bend wrist, not can; straw redirects.")
print("Liquid on board: let evaporate FULLY before power-on.")

title: Use Case: New-Build Pre-Assembly Blowout
description: New cases ship with metal shavings, foam bits, and packaging dust inside — blast the empty case before installing anything. Hit every corner, the PSU basement, and drive bays; the debris you remove now never becomes a short under the motherboard later. Two minutes with a duster before the build beats an hour of fault-hunting after.

t: How Many Cans a Shop Uses: Cost Planning
title: How Many Cans a Shop Uses: Cost Planning
description: A can gives roughly 50-100 good bursts — a few full cleanings. A home builder uses 2-4 cans a year; a repair shop can burn through a can a week. At 5-8 dollars a can, shops should price the electric duster alternative: a 60-80 dollar electric blower pays for itself in a few months of shop use and never runs out mid-job.

demo.program:
bursts, per_clean = 75, 20
print(f"Can: ~{bursts} bursts (~{bursts//per_clean} full cleanings).")
print("Home: 2-4 cans/year. Shop: ~1 can/week.")
print("Shop math: $70 electric blower pays for itself in months, never runs dry mid-job.")

t: Storage and Disposal of Duster Cans
title: Storage and Disposal of Duster Cans
description: Store cans upright in cool places — heat raises internal pressure, and a hot car can rupture a can. Never puncture or incinerate, even 'empty' (residual pressure remains). Dispose as hazardous/aerosol waste per local rules, not in regular trash. Keep away from children: the abuse warnings exist because the danger is real.

demo.program:
print("Store upright, cool (heat = pressure = rupture risk; never hot cars).")
print("Never puncture/incinerate, even 'empty'. Aerosol waste disposal, not trash.")
print("Away from children. The warnings are real.")

t: Compressed Air vs Electric Dusters vs Air Compressors
title: Compressed Air vs Electric Dusters vs Air Compressors
description: Canned air: portable, dry, precise — costs per use, chills with use. Electric dusters (like the DataVac): strong continuous blast, no chill, pays for itself in shops, bulkier. Shop air compressors: unlimited air but risk moisture and oil in the line — need filters/dryers, and unregulated pressure can damage fans. Home: cans. Shop: electric. Compressor: only with proper filtration.

demo.program:
print("canned   : portable, precise, dry | per-use cost, chills")
print("electric : continuous, no chill, shop-payback | bulkier upfront cost")
print("compressor: unlimited | moisture/oil risk, needs filters, pressure control")
print("Home: cans. Shop: electric. Compressor: filtered + regulated only.")

t: Buying Guide: What Matters in a Duster Can
title: Buying Guide: What Matters in a Duster Can
description: What matters: net weight (10 oz standard — lighter cans are worse value), a straw nozzle included, a trigger that meters well (not all-blast-or-nothing), and bitterant clearly labeled. Multipacks (3-6 cans) cut the per-can price nearly in half. For shops, skip to the electric duster decision instead of optimizing can purchases.

t: Environmental Notes: Propellants and Responsible Use
title: Environmental Notes: Propellants and Responsible Use
description: Modern dusters use HFC-134a or HFO-1234ze propellants — better than the old CFCs but still greenhouse gases, so every burst has a footprint. Responsible use: short bursts only where needed, electric dusters for heavy shop use, and never 'play' with the can. The greenest blast is the one you did not need because filters caught the dust first.

demo.program:
print("Propellants (HFC/HFO): better than CFCs, still greenhouse gases.")
print("Responsible: short bursts as needed; electric for shop volume.")
print("Greenest blast: the one filters made unnecessary. Maintain intake filters.")
